speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you're experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me determine the cause, could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and when it started? Also, did you experience any specific injury or repetitive activity before these symptoms began?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis, likely exacerbated by infant care and previous trauma.

Based on the pain location (thumb and wrist radiating to elbow) and worsening with holding your infant, I suspect inflammation of the thumb tendons. The history of falling on your hand six months ago may have caused underlying damage that is now symptomatic. Your mother's history with methotrexate suggests a potential autoimmune component, which could indicate Rheumatoid Arthritis as well. Given the specific location and mechanical aggravation, would you be able to perform Finkelstein's test by tucking your thumb into your fist and bending your wrist downward to see if it reproduces the sharp pain?
